extracted.intended_audience: students and researchers conducting critical appraisal of research studies (particularly in healthcare)
extracted.subtask_description: Using CASP (Critical Appraisal Skills Programme) checklists to evaluate the quality, results, and applicability of research studies across different study designs. Guides selection of the appropriate checklist and how to use checklist questions to structure and focus appraisal and evidence selection for assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are the results of the study valid?
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the three main sections around which CASP checklists are structured: 'Are the results of the study valid?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the checklist questions that probe study validity to ensure you've considered aspects that affect internal validity (e.g., study design strengths/limitations, bias, confounding). These validity questions form the first logical stage of appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: What are the results?
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the three main sections around which CASP checklists are structured: 'What are the results?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the checklist prompts to extract and evaluate the main findings, effect sizes, precision, and whether reported results address the stated question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Will the results help locally? (in my setting)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the three main sections around which CASP checklists are structured: 'Will the results help locally? (in my setting)'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess applicability/transferability of the results to your context — consider population, setting, feasibility, and relevance for local practice or policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the appropriate CASP checklist for the study type
rubrics_metrics.description: CASP checklists cover the following types of research methods: Systematic Reviews, Randomised Controlled Trials, Cohort Studies, Case Control Studies, Economic Evaluations, Diagnostic Studies, Qualitative studies, and Clinical Prediction Rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the checklist that matches the study's methodology so you consider the right set of questions; the page links to the CASP Checklists website for the specific checklists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat checklist questions as a logical but selective framework ('Do the groundwork but be selective')
rubrics_metrics.description: Think of the questions on the relevant CASP checklist as a logical way to evaluate the quality of evidence in each text that you read. Following the checklist helps you to do the necessary groundwork, but not everything you write in response to the CASP checklist will be relevant for your assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the checklist to structure and stimulate your thinking so you can decide which pieces of evidence are important to include and why; be selective about which checklist responses you report in an assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the checklist to structure your evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the appropriate checklist to help structure your evaluation of a research study to ensure you have considered all aspects of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the checklist systematically to avoid missing key aspects of study appraisal (validity, results, applicability), while tailoring which outputs you present to the needs of your assignment or decision-making context.
